source.title: A Generalized Information Bottleneck Theory of Deep Learning
source.authors: Charles Westphal; Stephen Hailes; Mirco Musolesi

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Reports an empirical association between a different measured property—synergy with augmentation noise—and generalization gap. It does not test the claim versions’ specified interventions or magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports information-plane compression dynamics and adversarial-attack results, but these do not measure the claim versions’ specified generalization outcomes. The extended-range test data for simple functions evaluates extrapolation, which is outside scope.
record.test_reason: The study measures augmentation-noise synergy and information-bottleneck dynamics, not any of V1–V8. Its generalization-gap correlation does not test V7 because it measures neither magnitude-aware weight sharpness nor its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors: they argue that synergistic functions generalize better and report smaller generalization gaps for CIFAR-10 ResNets with higher augmentation-noise synergy proxies. The empirical result is correlational and does not establish that increasing synergy causes better generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Measures synergy with augmentation noise using a teacher-student framework and correlates it with generalization gap; it does not reproduce the claim versions’ interventions or sharpness measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that information-plane dynamics vary with MI estimator and, for ResNets, with PCA dimensionality; these findings do not change the generalization-gap association reported in R1.

fits_no_version.finding: Across CIFAR-10 ResNet configurations, the teacher-student synergy proxy correlates negatively with generalization gap: Pearson r = −0.79, p < 0.001.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For CIFAR-10 ResNets trained with random crops and horizontal flips, a higher teacher-student proxy for augmentation-noise synergy is associated with a smaller generalization gap.

record.code_released: The paper says code will be made publicly available upon publication; no URL is stated.
record.problems: The generalization-gap association is reported only in aggregate across model configurations, with no per-model values or uncertainty interval; the text does not describe a control for the correlation.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results measure an outcome covered by the listed claim versions. The information-plane figures report dynamics rather than the versions’ named generalization outcomes; simple-function experiments evaluate extrapolation.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-versus-random-label held-out accuracy. BERT random-label unlearning reports information-plane dynamics without the required accuracy comparisons.
Width-dependent test error beyond the zero-training-error threshold; the ResNet experiments vary depth.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance under matched tuning conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out error, including interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Using SGD, AdamW, augmentation, or random-label training in separate experiments does not supply the comparisons required by the listed versions. No version-specific verdict is warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the effects of local connectivity.
Held-out performance comparisons among adaptive optimizers and SGD.
Large versus small batch performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: ResNet models of depths 20, 32, 44, 56, 68, 80, 92, and 110 (aggregate across configurations)
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 with standard data augmentations
rows.operation_detail: Measured synergy with augmentation noise and its association with generalization gap across model configurations.

conditions.value: teacher-student framework; synergy ratio I(f(X, ε); ε|X)/I(f(X, ε); X, ε)

rows.measure: Association between synergy measure and generalization gap
rows.note: The reported association is aggregate across all model configurations; no per-depth values are stated. The measure is synergy with augmentation noise, not magnitude-aware sharpness.
rows.check: The reported correlation is correctly transcribed, but cannot establish any listed version. Describe the predictor as a teacher-student cross-entropy/entropy proxy that the authors interpret as an upper bound on the synergy ratio, rather than a direct synergy measurement.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
